resources.string: Two emoji as one sticker, from a source you add
Add a source to use this.
Pick an emoji to see a row of mixes with it
When you pick an emoji in the emoji panel, a row above the panel shows mixes made with that emoji. A tap sends one. This setting is on by default.
When the text ends in one or two emoji
When your text ends in one or two emoji, the suggestion strip offers mixes of them. A tap sends the mix as a sticker or a picture.

How the suggestion strip offers emoji mixes. Thumbnails shows small pictures of the mixes on the strip itself. One chip shows a single button that opens the mixes. A row above adds a separate row of mixes over the strip. The default is Thumbnails.
Sending a mix removes the emoji it was made from
When you send a mix, the keyboard deletes the emoji that you typed to make it, so the message holds the mix only. With this off, the emoji stay in your text. This setting is on by default.
A tab beside emoji, GIFs and stickers to put any two emoji together
Adds a Mixes tab beside emoji, GIFs and stickers. There you pick any two emoji and get their mix, without typing them first.
The order of the mixes offered for an emoji. As the source has them keeps the order of the list they come from. Your emoji first puts the mixes with the emoji you use most at the front.
Apps that take no stickers get a picture
How a mix is sent. A sticker has a clear background and shows large in apps that take stickers. A picture works in every app. An app that takes no stickers always gets a picture.
The size of each mix in the Mixes panel. Larger mixes are easier to see, and fewer fit on the screen. The default is 72 dp.
Only on a connection that is not metered
Downloads the lists of mixes again once a month, to pick up new ones. The download runs only on Wi-Fi or another connection that does not count data. This setting is off by default.
